title: AI Model Family Atlas
description: Selected public model-family releases and relationships from major developers. Links show succession, variants, distillation or comparable branches, not claims of shared training data.

curriculumPresets.title: Full AI model atlas
curriculumPresets.description: Explore selected model families, release cadence, open-weight branches and cross-family distillation links.

curriculumPresets.title: Current model landscape
curriculumPresets.description: Focus on 2026 releases and verify status from linked developer sources before making capability comparisons.

curriculumPresets.title: Open-weight ecosystems
curriculumPresets.description: Compare Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek and gpt-oss. Distinguish downloadable weights from open-source software and open training data.

curriculumPresets.title: Reasoning model branches
curriculumPresets.description: Trace reasoning-oriented releases and distillation links. Evaluate benchmark claims alongside task design, cost and deployment constraints.

curriculumPresets.title: Responsible AI investigation
curriculumPresets.description: Use release notes as claims to verify, then investigate licensing, privacy, bias, energy, safety evaluation and acceptable-use constraints.

curriculumPresets.title: Model provenance and distillation
curriculumPresets.description: Trace base models, specialist branches and DeepSeek-R1 distillation links. Record developer, checkpoint, licence and transformation evidence.

curriculumPresets.title: AI for software development
curriculumPresets.description: Compare general models with specialist code branches such as Codestral, Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder using tests and repository-level tasks.

curriculumPresets.title: Multimodal model branches
curriculumPresets.description: Investigate omni, vision and edge variants. Build an evaluation that requires grounded use of image or audio input.

sources.label: OpenAI: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
OpenAI: Learning to reason with LLMs

nodes.name: AI Model Families
nodes.note: This map samples public releases from several developers. A successor line does not imply identical architecture, data or evaluation.
nodes.hook: Choose a capability claim and follow its source before treating it as evidence.

nodes.name: OpenAI GPT
nodes.note: The GPT family includes hosted frontier releases and a separate open-weight gpt-oss branch.
nodes.hook: Distinguish product names, API model IDs and downloadable model weights.

nodes.name: GPT-4 generation
nodes.note: GPT-4 and multimodal variants preceded the unified GPT-5 line.
nodes.hook: Compare a generation label with a specific dated model snapshot.

nodes.name: GPT-5
nodes.note: GPT-5 introduced a unified system spanning fast and deeper reasoning behaviour.
nodes.hook: Separate developer capability claims from independently reproducible evaluation.

nodes.name: GPT-5.5
nodes.note: GPT-5.5 extended the hosted GPT-5 family in April 2026.
nodes.hook: Build a test set tied to a real task before comparing versions.

nodes.name: GPT-5.6 family
nodes.note: GPT-5.6 launched as a family in July 2026.
nodes.hook: Explain why a family name may cover models with different speed and capability targets.

nodes.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
nodes.note: A fast, economical member of the GPT-5.6 family.
nodes.hook: Choose a latency-sensitive task and define an acceptable quality threshold.

nodes.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
nodes.note: A balanced GPT-5.6 family member.
nodes.hook: Compare total workflow cost rather than token price alone.

nodes.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
nodes.note: A frontier capability member of the GPT-5.6 family.
nodes.hook: Identify when additional capability is worth greater latency or cost.

nodes.name: gpt-oss
nodes.note: OpenAI released downloadable open-weight reasoning models in 2025.
nodes.hook: Distinguish open weights, source code, training data and licence permissions.

nodes.name: Anthropic Claude
nodes.note: Claude uses capability tiers and dated generation releases across hosted models.
nodes.hook: Compare tier naming with version numbering before selecting a model.

nodes.name: Claude 3 generation
nodes.note: Claude 3 established Haiku, Sonnet and Opus tier names.
nodes.hook: Explain how tier and generation answer different selection questions.

nodes.name: Claude 4
nodes.note: Claude 4 launched with Sonnet and Opus variants.
nodes.hook: Compare release-note claims using one controlled prompt set.

nodes.name: Claude Opus 4.6
nodes.note: Opus 4.6 was announced in February 2026.
nodes.hook: Record model version and date so an evaluation can be reproduced.

nodes.name: Claude Opus 4.8
nodes.note: Opus 4.8 followed in May 2026.
nodes.hook: Investigate what changed between two point releases rather than inferring from numbering.

nodes.name: Claude Opus 5
nodes.note: Opus 5 was announced in July 2026.
nodes.hook: Assess suitability using task accuracy, safety, latency and cost.

nodes.name: Google Gemini
nodes.note: Gemini is a multimodal family delivered through products and developer APIs.
nodes.hook: Separate a model family announcement from an API availability state.

nodes.name: Gemini 1.0
nodes.note: The original Gemini launch presented Ultra, Pro and Nano variants.
nodes.hook: Match variant scale to device and service constraints.

nodes.name: Gemini 1.5
nodes.note: Gemini 1.5 developed the family’s long-context and multimodal direction.
nodes.hook: Design a test that measures useful retrieval rather than context-window size alone.

nodes.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
nodes.note: Gemini 2.5 Pro is documented as a reasoning-capable multimodal model.
nodes.hook: Verify current lifecycle status on the model documentation page.

nodes.name: Gemini 3
nodes.note: Gemini 3 extended the developer API family.
nodes.hook: Compare a preview identifier with a stable identifier before production use.

nodes.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
nodes.note: Gemini 3.7 Flash documentation was current in August 2026.
nodes.hook: Evaluate a fast model on throughput and failure cost, not speed alone.

nodes.name: Meta Llama
nodes.note: Llama is a downloadable model-weight family with licence terms that must be checked per release.
nodes.hook: Audit licence, hardware and data-governance constraints before deployment.

nodes.name: Llama 2
nodes.note: Llama 2 broadened the public model-weight family.
nodes.hook: Explain why downloadable does not automatically mean unrestricted.

nodes.name: Llama 3
nodes.note: Llama 3 introduced a new generation of pretrained and instruction-tuned weights.
nodes.hook: Compare base and instruction-tuned purposes.

nodes.name: Llama 3.1
nodes.note: Llama 3.1 expanded the family and included a 405B model.
nodes.hook: Estimate deployment requirements before comparing headline capability.

nodes.name: Llama 4
nodes.note: Llama 4 introduced multimodal mixture-of-experts models.
nodes.hook: Separate total parameters from active parameters when interpreting architecture.

nodes.name: Mistral AI
nodes.note: Mistral publishes both open-weight and hosted commercial model lines.
nodes.hook: Classify each model by access method and licence, not developer name alone.

nodes.name: Mistral 7B
nodes.note: Mistral 7B established the developer’s compact open-weight line.
nodes.hook: Test whether model size predicts performance on your chosen task.

nodes.name: Mixtral
nodes.note: Mixtral developed a sparse mixture-of-experts branch.
nodes.hook: Explain active versus total parameters with a resource budget.

nodes.name: Mistral 3
nodes.note: Mistral 3 is a family spanning small and frontier-scale releases.
nodes.hook: Compare a family portfolio rather than treating one score as universal.

nodes.name: Mistral Small 4
nodes.note: Mistral Small 4 continued the compact model line in 2026.
nodes.hook: Define a local-deployment scenario and test memory, speed and quality.

nodes.name: Alibaba Qwen
nodes.note: Qwen has public multilingual and multimodal model-weight families.
nodes.hook: Verify model card, licence and intended use for a specific checkpoint.

nodes.name: Qwen
nodes.note: The original Qwen release began the public family.
nodes.hook: Use the technical blog to identify stated languages and evaluation scope.

nodes.name: Qwen2
nodes.note: Qwen2 expanded the family’s model sizes and multilingual support.
nodes.hook: Compare a base checkpoint with an instruction-tuned checkpoint.

nodes.name: Qwen2.5
nodes.note: Qwen2.5 developed specialist and general model variants.
nodes.hook: Select a specialist model only after checking domain and output requirements.

nodes.name: Qwen3
nodes.note: Qwen3 introduced hybrid thinking modes across a broad model family.
nodes.hook: Test when explicit reasoning improves or harms task efficiency.

nodes.name: DeepSeek
nodes.note: DeepSeek includes general, code and reasoning releases, plus distilled checkpoints based on other model families.
nodes.hook: Trace model provenance and licences when a checkpoint is distilled from another family.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-V3
nodes.note: V3 established the general mixture-of-experts branch used alongside reasoning releases.
nodes.hook: Compare general and reasoning-tuned model purposes.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-R1
nodes.note: R1 is a reasoning release accompanied by distilled Qwen- and Llama-based checkpoints.
nodes.hook: Explain distillation without describing the student model as a direct successor.

nodes.name: R1-Distill-Qwen
nodes.note: Distilled reasoning checkpoints use Qwen base models in several sizes.
nodes.hook: Follow both source families when documenting provenance and licence constraints.

nodes.name: R1-Distill-Llama
nodes.note: Distilled reasoning checkpoints also use Llama base models.
nodes.hook: Compare distillation with fine-tuning and retrieval augmentation.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-V3.1
nodes.note: V3.1 developed the general/hybrid line in August 2025.
nodes.hook: Record exact API or checkpoint version when testing.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-V4 Pro
nodes.note: DeepSeek announced V4 Pro in August 2026.
nodes.hook: Treat a vendor announcement as a starting point for evaluation, not a conclusion.

nodes.name: GPT-3
nodes.note: GPT-3 demonstrated large-scale few-shot language modelling before the ChatGPT product era.
nodes.hook: Compare research model, product interface and API deployment as distinct layers.

nodes.name: GPT-3.5 / ChatGPT launch
nodes.note: GPT-3.5 models powered the early public ChatGPT launch period.
nodes.hook: Explain how a product launch can increase impact without being a new base-model generation.

nodes.name: GPT-4
nodes.note: GPT-4 established the generation later expanded through Turbo and multimodal variants.
nodes.hook: Record exact model identifiers instead of treating GPT-4 as one immutable model.

nodes.name: GPT-4o
nodes.note: GPT-4o introduced an omni multimodal branch across text, image and audio interactions.
nodes.hook: Create a modality matrix showing input, output and evaluation requirements.

nodes.name: OpenAI o1
nodes.note: o1 made test-time reasoning a distinct named model branch.
nodes.hook: Compare answer quality and compute cost on problems that do and do not benefit from deliberation.

nodes.name: OpenAI o3
nodes.note: o3 continued the reasoning-series branch before GPT-5 unified model routing.
nodes.hook: Avoid comparing benchmark scores without matching tools and reasoning settings.

nodes.name: gpt-oss-20b
nodes.note: The smaller gpt-oss checkpoint targets more accessible local or specialised deployment.
nodes.hook: Estimate memory needs at two quantisation levels before selecting hardware.

nodes.name: gpt-oss-120b
nodes.note: The larger gpt-oss checkpoint increases deployment demands.
nodes.hook: Compare throughput, memory and evaluation quality against the 20B variant.

nodes.name: Claude 1
nodes.note: Claude 1 began Anthropic’s public hosted model family.
nodes.hook: Build a release timeline using dated announcements rather than product recollection.

nodes.name: Claude 2
nodes.note: Claude 2 expanded the early family before tiered Claude 3 models.
nodes.hook: Identify which capability claims are no longer meaningful for a retired model.

nodes.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
nodes.note: Claude 3.5 Sonnet was a major mid-generation capability update.
nodes.hook: Explain why decimal generation labels can still represent material changes.

nodes.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
nodes.note: Sonnet 4.6 was a cost-performance branch of the Claude 4 generation.
nodes.hook: Compare a tier change with a generation change.

nodes.name: Claude Fable 5
nodes.note: Fable 5 is a Claude 5 tier aimed at broad professional work.
nodes.hook: Check current access and safeguards before planning classroom use.

nodes.name: Claude Mythos 5
nodes.note: Mythos 5 is a high-capability Claude 5 tier with stronger cyber safeguards and access considerations.
nodes.hook: Discuss why capability-sensitive safeguards may differ between tiers.

nodes.name: Claude Sonnet 5
nodes.note: Sonnet 5 extends the fifth-generation cost-performance range.
nodes.hook: Test a representative workflow instead of assuming tier names map directly across generations.

nodes.name: Gemini 1.5 Flash
nodes.note: Flash created a throughput-oriented branch of Gemini 1.5.
nodes.hook: Compare latency, context use and error cost on a high-volume task.

nodes.name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
nodes.note: Gemini 2.0 Flash developed the fast multimodal API line.
nodes.hook: Separate preview, experimental and stable API identifiers.

nodes.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
nodes.note: Gemini 3.6 Flash preceded 3.7 as a stable Flash generation.
nodes.hook: Use model lifecycle status to plan migration windows.

nodes.name: Google Gemma
nodes.note: Gemma is Google’s separate downloadable open-model family.
nodes.hook: Distinguish Gemini hosted models from Gemma downloadable weights.

nodes.name: Gemma 3
nodes.note: Gemma 3 expanded the open-model family with multimodal and size variants.
nodes.hook: Choose a checkpoint using licence, modality and device constraints.

nodes.name: LLaMA
nodes.note: The original research release preceded the more broadly licensed Llama 2 family.
nodes.hook: Compare research access with production licence permissions.

nodes.name: Llama 3.2
nodes.note: Llama 3.2 added vision and smaller edge-oriented variants.
nodes.hook: Match a model size and modality to an edge-device constraint.

nodes.name: Codestral
nodes.note: Codestral is a specialist code-model branch rather than a general chat successor.
nodes.hook: Evaluate repository completion and explanation tasks separately.

nodes.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
nodes.note: Medium 3.5 is a hosted mid-tier model release from May 2026.
nodes.hook: Compare hosted and downloadable deployment constraints.

nodes.name: Qwen-VL
nodes.note: Qwen-VL is the family’s vision-language branch.
nodes.hook: Create an evaluation containing image-grounded questions that cannot be solved from text alone.

nodes.name: Qwen2.5-Coder
nodes.note: Qwen2.5-Coder is a specialist coding branch in multiple sizes.
nodes.hook: Compare code completion, repair and explanation as separate tasks.

nodes.name: QwQ
nodes.note: QwQ explored a reasoning-oriented branch before Qwen3 hybrid thinking.
nodes.hook: Compare dedicated reasoning with Qwen3 selectable thinking modes.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-Coder
nodes.note: DeepSeek-Coder is the specialist programming branch.
nodes.hook: Measure generated-code correctness with tests rather than style impressions.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
nodes.note: V3.2 followed V3.1 in December 2025.
nodes.hook: Pin API or checkpoint versions when evaluating rapid release lines.

nodes.name: DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision Experimental
nodes.note: An experimental vision-capable V4 Flash branch was announced in August 2026.
nodes.hook: Keep experimental models out of critical workflows until lifecycle and evaluation are clear.
